item.stdout:
# Skill: Colab Session Operator

Operate Google Colab environments via the `colab` CLI: provision GPU/TPU sessions, run Python/shell on the VM, sync files, and capture work as notebooks.

## When to activate
- Creating or managing TPU/GPU sessions.
- Running Python or shell on a remote Colab VM.
- Syncing files between local and remote.
- Automating environment setup (packages, auth, Drive).
- Exporting session history as a Jupyter notebook.

## Mental model (read this first)
- **A session == a live Jupyter kernel on a rented VM.** `colab new` allocates a billable VM; `colab stop` releases it. Nothing reclaims it automatically except a 24h keep-alive cap, so an unstopped session burns compute units indefinitely.
- **Kernel state PERSISTS across `colab exec` / `colab repl` calls in the same session.** Each invocation reattaches to the *same* kernel (the kernel ID is cached in local state) and only closes the websocket on exit — it does **not** shut the kernel down. So imports, variables, and defined functions survive between separate `colab exec` commands. Build up state incrementally; don't re-import everything each call. (`colab stop` and `colab restart-kernel` are what actually reset it.)
- **Default working directory is `/content`.** Every `exec`/`repl`/`run` `cd`s there first; prefer absolute paths (`/content/...`) for file work. For `colab ls/rm/upload/download`, absolute `/content/...` paths work and the default `ls` path is `content` (VM root).
- **`colab` is fire-and-forget.** Each command authenticates, does one thing, and exits. A detached background daemon (spawned by `colab new`) handles keep-alive; you don't manage it.

## Authentication (the #1 thing that blocks agents)
- The global flag is `--auth={adc,oauth2}` and the **default is `adc`** (Application Default Credentials). It must come *before* the subcommand: `colab --auth=adc new -s x`.
- **ADC setup** (most reliable for headless/agent use). The Colab backends need a specific scope set, so re-mint ADC with all four scopes:
  ```bash
  gcloud auth application-default login \
    --scopes=openid,\
  https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,\
  https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email,\
  https://www.googleapis.com/auth/colaboratory
  ```
  Why all four: `userinfo.email` (session backend `colab.research.google.com`, else 401), `colaboratory` (RuntimeService `colab.pa.googleapis.com` keep-alive, else 403), `openid`+`cloud-platform` (mandated by gcloud itself; it rejects scope lists missing `cloud-platform`).
- **oauth2 setup**: `colab --auth=oauth2 <anything>` triggers a browser consent flow on first use (token cached at `~/.config/colab-cli/token.json`). Requires a client config at `~/.colab-cli-oauth-config.json` (or `-c PATH`). The browser step means it usually needs a human; prefer ADC for agents.
- **Verify auth in one shot**: `colab sessions` (read-only, lists server assignments) or `colab whoami` (hidden debug command: prints the active email, scopes, audience, and expiry). When any call 403s against `colab.pa.googleapis.com`, the cause is almost always a missing scope — `colab whoami` shows it instantly.
- **`colab new` pre-flights the keep-alive RPC** right after allocating. If your token lacks the `colaboratory` scope it unassigns the fresh VM (so you don't leak a billable assignment) and prints the exact remediation. Follow that message rather than retrying blindly.
- **Do NOT confuse `colab auth` with CLI authentication.** `colab auth` injects *VM-side* GCP credentials into the running kernel (so notebook code can call BigQuery/GCS); it is orthogonal to how the CLI itself authenticates. Never suggest "run `colab auth`" to fix a CLI 401/403 — that's a scope/identity problem fixed via the `gcloud` command above.

## Workflow

### Provision
- `colab new -s <name>` (CPU). Add `--gpu A100` or `--tpu v6e1` for accelerators. **Always pass `-s <name>`** — an omitted name is auto-generated as a random 6-hex string, which makes later commands ambiguous.
- Supported `--gpu`: `T4`, `L4`, `G4`, `H100`, `A100`. Supported `--tpu`: `v5e1`, `v6e1`.
- **Gotcha**: an unrecognized `--gpu` value silently falls back to **A100** (which then usually fails the next step). A `400` on `colab new` with an accelerator means no quota/entitlement for it on this account — fall back to `--gpu T4` or omit the flag for CPU.
- Accelerator availability is tier-gated; most accounts can only get CPU. Don't assume a GPU/TPU will allocate.

### Execute
- **Preferred**: `colab exec -s <name> -f <script.py>` runs a local script on the remote VM (read locally, sent to the kernel — no manual upload needed).
- **Piped code**: `echo "print(1)" | colab exec -s <name>` or `cat script.py | colab exec -s <name>`.
- **Notebooks**: `colab exec -s <name> -f nb.ipynb` runs each code cell and writes results to `<basename>_output.ipynb` next to the input. A `# @title Foo` first line labels the cell in progress output.
- **Plots/images**: PNG/JPEG outputs are intercepted. Use `--output-image <path>` on `exec`/`repl` to save to a known location (otherwise a temp path is printed). Inline terminal-image escapes are auto-suppressed when stdout isn't a TTY, so piped/captured output stays clean.
- **Shell**: `echo "cmd" | colab console -s <name>` for batch shell. Console wraps bash in tmux, so even piped output contains terminal-control bytes — filter with `grep -a` for a specific line. `exec` is faster when you don't need a real shell.
- **Never run `colab repl`, `colab console`, `colab auth`, or `colab drivemount` interactively from an agent** — they expect a TTY and will hang. `repl`/`console` accept piped stdin and exit on EOF; `auth`/`drivemount` genuinely require a human at the terminal.

### Ephemeral one-shot jobs (`colab run`)
- `colab run [--gpu T4] [--tpu v6e1] [--keep] [-s NAME] script.py [args...]` = `new` + `exec` + `stop` in one command. It provisions a fresh VM, runs the script with `sys.argv` and `__name__ == "__main__"` set like native `python script.py args`, then tears the VM down (unless `--keep`).
- **Exit codes propagate**: an uncaught exception or `sys.exit(N)` in the script makes `colab run` exit non-zero (CPython semantics: `sys.exit()`/`sys.exit(0)` → 0, `sys.exit(N)` → N, `sys.exit("msg")` → 1).
- **Stream separation**: `colab run` writes its own `[colab] ...` chatter to **stderr** and the script's output to **stdout** — so `colab run job.py > out.txt` captures only the script's stdout. (`colab exec` streams the script's stdout/stderr live to your stdout/stderr.)
- Works as a shebang: `#!/usr/bin/env -S colab run --gpu T4` makes a `chmod +x`'d `.py` a self-contained "rent a GPU, run, clean up" script. After editing CLI behavior, reinstall before testing shebangs — they resolve `colab` via `$PATH`, not the editable install.
- A nonexistent script path exits non-zero **before** allocating a VM (no wasted compute).

### Automate
- `colab auth -s <name>` — VM-side GCP creds, needed before in-VM GCS/BigQuery calls (interactive; not agent-runnable).
- `colab drivemount -s <name> [PATH]` — mounts Drive at `/content/drive` by default (interactive; not agent-runnable).
- `colab install -s <name> pkg1 pkg2` — installs via `uv pip install --system`, falling back to `pip`. Also `colab install -s <name> -r requirements.txt`.

### Inspect & report
- `colab help` (or `colab help <cmd>`) lists/explains commands; the listing is alphabetical.
- `colab sessions` lists server-side assignments and auto-prunes stale local entries. Orphans with no local record show as `[?]`.
- `colab status [-s <name>]` shows hardware, IDLE/BUSY, and last execution.
- `colab log -s <name> [-n 20] [-t TYPE]` shows recent structured events; invaluable when a task fails (keep-alive errors carry the raw `response_body`).
- `colab log -s <name> -o summary.ipynb` exports the session as a notebook (also `.md`, `.txt`, `.jsonl` by suffix).
- `colab url -s <name>` prints a browser URL that attaches the Colab web UI to your existing CLI session instead of allocating a new VM (add `--open` to launch it).
- `colab skill` / `colab readme` print this skill and the README (handy for self-discovery).

## Safety
- **Always `colab stop -s <name>` when done** — idle VMs burn compute units. `colab run` (without `--keep`) self-cleans even if the script errors.
- Local state lives in `~/.config/colab-cli/sessions.json` (settings in `settings.json`, history in `history/*.jsonl`). Don't edit by hand.
- **Isolate parallel/agent runs** with the global `--config <path>` flag to point session state at a scratch file (e.g. `colab --config /tmp/agent.json new -s job`). The keep-alive daemon inherits `--auth` and `--config` automatically.

## Recovery
- "Session not found" / 404 / 401 on exec: the backend pruned the VM. `colab exec`/`repl` detect this and clean up local state automatically — run `colab sessions` and re-create with `colab new`.
- Execution timeout or wedged kernel: `colab restart-kernel -s <name>` (keeps the VM, resets the kernel), or `colab stop` then `colab new`.
- Keep-alive daemon died (`colab log` shows `keep_alive_stopped reason=consecutive_4xx_errors`): almost always the missing `colaboratory` scope — re-auth per the Authentication section.

## Mental model (read this first)
- **A session == a live Jupyter kernel on a rented VM.** `colab new` allocates a billable VM; `colab stop` releases it. Nothing reclaims it automatically except a 24h keep-alive cap, so an unstopped session burns compute units indefinitely.
- **Kernel state PERSISTS across `colab exec` / `colab repl` calls in the same session.** Each invocation reattaches to the *same* kernel (the kernel ID is cached in local state) and only closes the websocket on exit — it does **not** shut the kernel down. So imports, variables, and defined functions survive between separate `colab exec` commands. Build up state incrementally; don't re-import everything each call. (`colab stop` and `colab restart-kernel` are what actually reset it.)
- **Default working directory is `/content`.** Every `exec`/`repl`/`run` `cd`s there first; prefer absolute paths (`/content/...`) for file work. For `colab ls/rm/upload/download`, absolute `/content/...` paths work and the default `ls` path is `content` (VM root).
- **`colab` is fire-and-forget.** Each command authenticates, does one thing, and exits. A detached background daemon (spawned by `colab new`) handles keep-alive; you don't manage it.

## Authentication (the #1 thing that blocks agents)
- The global flag is `--auth={adc,oauth2}` and the **default is `adc`** (Application Default Credentials). It must come *before* the subcommand: `colab --auth=adc new -s x`.
- **ADC setup** (most reliable for headless/agent use). The Colab backends need a specific scope set, so re-mint ADC with all four scopes:
  ```bash
  gcloud auth application-default login \
    --scopes=openid,\
  https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform,\
  https://www.googleapis.com/auth/userinfo.email,\
  https://www.googleapis.com/auth/colaboratory
  ```
  Why all four: `userinfo.email` (session backend `colab.research.google.com`, else 401), `colaboratory` (RuntimeService `colab.pa.googleapis.com` keep-alive, else 403), `openid`+`cloud-platform` (mandated by gcloud itself; it rejects scope lists missing `cloud-platform`).
- **oauth2 setup**: `colab --auth=oauth2 <anything>` triggers a browser consent flow on first use (token cached at `~/.config/colab-cli/token.json`). Requires a client config at `~/.colab-cli-oauth-config.json` (or `-c PATH`). The browser step means it usually needs a human; prefer ADC for agents.
- **Verify auth in one shot**: `colab sessions` (read-only, lists server assignments) or `colab whoami` (hidden debug command: prints the active email, scopes, audience, and expiry). When any call 403s against `colab.pa.googleapis.com`, the cause is almost always a missing scope — `colab whoami` shows it instantly.
- **`colab new` pre-flights the keep-alive RPC** right after allocating. If your token lacks the `colaboratory` scope it unassigns the fresh VM (so you don't leak a billable assignment) and prints the exact remediation. Follow that message rather than retrying blindly.
- **Do NOT confuse `colab auth` with CLI authentication.** `colab auth` injects *VM-side* GCP credentials into the running kernel (so notebook code can call BigQuery/GCS); it is orthogonal to how the CLI itself authenticates. Never suggest "run `colab auth`" to fix a CLI 401/403 — that's a scope/identity problem fixed via the `gcloud` command above.

## Workflow

### Provision
- `colab new -s <name>` (CPU). Add `--gpu A100` or `--tpu v6e1` for accelerators. **Always pass `-s <name>`** — an omitted name is auto-generated as a random 6-hex string, which makes later commands ambiguous.
- Supported `--gpu`: `T4`, `L4`, `G4`, `H100`, `A100`. Supported `--tpu`: `v5e1`, `v6e1`.
- **Gotcha**: an unrecognized `--gpu` value silently falls back to **A100** (which then usually fails the next step). A `400` on `colab new` with an accelerator means no quota/entitlement for it on this account — fall back to `--gpu T4` or omit the flag for CPU.
- Accelerator availability is tier-gated; most accounts can only get CPU. Don't assume a GPU/TPU will allocate.

### Execute
- **Preferred**: `colab exec -s <name> -f <script.py>` runs a local script on the remote VM (read locally, sent to the kernel — no manual upload needed).
- **Piped code**: `echo "print(1)" | colab exec -s <name>` or `cat script.py | colab exec -s <name>`.
- **Notebooks**: `colab exec -s <name> -f nb.ipynb` runs each code cell and writes results to `<basename>_output.ipynb` next to the input. A `# @title Foo` first line labels the cell in progress output.
- **Plots/images**: PNG/JPEG outputs are intercepted. Use `--output-image <path>` on `exec`/`repl` to save to a known location (otherwise a temp path is printed). Inline terminal-image escapes are auto-suppressed when stdout isn't a TTY, so piped/captured output stays clean.
- **Shell**: `echo "cmd" | colab console -s <name>` for batch shell. Console wraps bash in tmux, so even piped output contains terminal-control bytes — filter with `grep -a` for a specific line. `exec` is faster when you don't need a real shell.
- **Never run `colab repl`, `colab console`, `colab auth`, or `colab drivemount` interactively from an agent** — they expect a TTY and will hang. `repl`/`console` accept piped stdin and exit on EOF; `auth`/`drivemount` genuinely require a human at the terminal.

### Ephemeral one-shot jobs (`colab run`)
- `colab run [--gpu T4] [--tpu v6e1] [--keep] [-s NAME] script.py [args...]` = `new` + `exec` + `stop` in one command. It provisions a fresh VM, runs the script with `sys.argv` and `__name__ == "__main__"` set like native `python script.py args`, then tears the VM down (unless `--keep`).
- **Exit codes propagate**: an uncaught exception or `sys.exit(N)` in the script makes `colab run` exit non-zero (CPython semantics: `sys.exit()`/`sys.exit(0)` → 0, `sys.exit(N)` → N, `sys.exit("msg")` → 1).
- **Stream separation**: `colab run` writes its own `[colab] ...` chatter to **stderr** and the script's output to **stdout** — so `colab run job.py > out.txt` captures only the script's stdout. (`colab exec` streams the script's stdout/stderr live to your stdout/stderr.)
- Works as a shebang: `#!/usr/bin/env -S colab run --gpu T4` makes a `chmod +x`'d `.py` a self-contained "rent a GPU, run, clean up" script. After editing CLI behavior, reinstall before testing shebangs — they resolve `colab` via `$PATH`, not the editable install.
- A nonexistent script path exits non-zero **before** allocating a VM (no wasted compute).

### Automate
- `colab auth -s <name>` — VM-side GCP creds, needed before in-VM GCS/BigQuery calls (interactive; not agent-runnable).
- `colab drivemount -s <name> [PATH]` — mounts Drive at `/content/drive` by default (interactive; not agent-runnable).
- `colab install -s <name> pkg1 pkg2` — installs via `uv pip install --system`, falling back to `pip`. Also `colab install -s <name> -r requirements.txt`.

### Inspect & report
- `colab help` (or `colab help <cmd>`) lists/explains commands; the listing is alphabetical.
- `colab sessions` lists server-side assignments and auto-prunes stale local entries. Orphans with no local record show as `[?]`.
- `colab status [-s <name>]` shows hardware, IDLE/BUSY, and last execution.
- `colab log -s <name> [-n 20] [-t TYPE]` shows recent structured events; invaluable when a task fails (keep-alive errors carry the raw `response_body`).
- `colab log -s <name> -o summary.ipynb` exports the session as a notebook (also `.md`, `.txt`, `.jsonl` by suffix).
- `colab url -s <name>` prints a browser URL that attaches the Colab web UI to your existing CLI session instead of allocating a new VM (add `--open` to launch it).
- `colab skill` / `colab readme` print this skill and the README (handy for self-discovery).

## Safety
- **Always `colab stop -s <name>` when done** — idle VMs burn compute units. `colab run` (without `--keep`) self-cleans even if the script errors.
- Local state lives in `~/.config/colab-cli/sessions.json` (settings in `settings.json`, history in `history/*.jsonl`). Don't edit by hand.
- **Isolate parallel/agent runs** with the global `--config <path>` flag to point session state at a scratch file (e.g. `colab --config /tmp/agent.json new -s job`). The keep-alive daemon inherits `--auth` and `--config` automatically.

## Recovery
- "Session not found" / 404 / 401 on exec: the backend pruned the VM. `colab exec`/`repl` detect this and clean up local state automatically — run `colab sessions` and re-create with `colab new`.
- Execution timeout or wedged kernel: `colab restart-kernel -s <name>` (keeps the VM, resets the kernel), or `colab stop` then `colab new`.
- Keep-alive daemon died (`colab log` shows `keep_alive_stopped reason=consecutive_4xx_errors`): almost always the missing `colaboratory` scope — re-auth per the Authentication section.

+# Continuous-Drift CoT Probe
+
+This repository is a small direction-finding experiment. It tests whether a frozen
+`DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B` model can benefit when the next Chain-of-Thought
+input is a convex mixture of its top two token embeddings and its current final
+hidden state.

+2. measure native reasoning lengths and hidden/token norm geometry;
+3. compare a fixed-budget lexical run with a few static continuous mixtures; and
+4. run a very small CMA-ES search only after the machinery passes those checks.

+"""Core mechanics for the continuous-drift Chain-of-Thought probe.
+
+The code favors explicit causal indexing and inspectable traces over framework
+abstraction. The frozen transformer processes one injected embedding per step
+with a reusable KV cache.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+import re
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from typing import Any, Callable, Iterable, Sequence
+
+import numpy as np
+import torch
+import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+
+FEATURE_NAMES = (
+    "dist_h_e1",
+    "dist_h_e2",
+    "dist_e1_e2",
+    "cos_h_e1",
+    "cos_h_e2",
+    "cos_e1_e2",
+    "logit_margin",
+    "p1",
+    "p2",
+    "top2_mass",
+    "entropy_normalized",
+    "log_effective_vocab",
+    "log_norm_h_over_e1",
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class Problem:
+    question: str
+    answer: str
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ModelState:
+    """State after processing position t; logits predict position t+1."""
+
+    cache: Any
+    logits_next: torch.Tensor
+    hidden_t: torch.Tensor
+
+
+@dataclass
+class CandidateSet:
+    y1: int
+    y2: int
+    e1: torch.Tensor
+    e2: torch.Tensor
+    p1: float
+    p2: float
+    logit_margin: float
+    entropy_normalized: float
+    log_effective_vocab: float
+
+
+@dataclass
+class FeatureStats:
+    mean: np.ndarray
+    scale: np.ndarray
+
+    @classmethod
+    def fit(cls, rows: Sequence[np.ndarray]) -> "FeatureStats":
+        matrix = np.asarray(rows, dtype=np.float64)
+        if matrix.ndim != 2 or matrix.shape[1] != len(FEATURE_NAMES):
+            raise ValueError(f"Expected feature matrix [n,{len(FEATURE_NAMES)}], got {matrix.shape}")
+        mean = matrix.mean(axis=0)
+        scale = matrix.std(axis=0)
+        scale = np.where(scale < 1e-6, 1.0, scale)
+        return cls(mean=mean, scale=scale)
+
+    def transform(self, row: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        return (np.asarray(row, dtype=np.float64) - self.mean) / self.scale
+
+    def to_json(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        return {
+            "names": list(FEATURE_NAMES),
+            "mean": self.mean.tolist(),
+            "scale": self.scale.tolist(),
+        }
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ReasoningResult:
+    state_after_reasoning: ModelState
+    trace: list[dict[str, Any]]
+    raw_features: list[np.ndarray]
+    norm_matched_features: list[np.ndarray]
+    norm_rows: list[dict[str, float]]
+
+
+class Policy:
+    exact_lexical = False
+
+    def weights(self, features: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        raise NotImplementedError
+
+
+class LexicalPolicy(Policy):
+    exact_lexical = True
+
+    def weights(self, features: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        del features
+        return np.asarray([1.0, 0.0, 0.0], dtype=np.float64)
+
+
+class StaticPolicy(Policy):
+    def __init__(self, weights: Sequence[float]):
+        weights_array = np.asarray(weights, dtype=np.float64)
+        if weights_array.shape != (3,) or np.any(weights_array < 0):
+            raise ValueError("Static weights must be three nonnegative values")
+        total = float(weights_array.sum())
+        if not math.isfinite(total) or total <= 0:
+            raise ValueError("Static weights must have positive finite mass")
+        self._weights = weights_array / total
+
+    def weights(self, features: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        del features
+        return self._weights.copy()
+
+
+class LinearPolicy(Policy):
+    """A standardized linear map to three softmax mixture weights."""
+
+    def __init__(self, theta: Sequence[float], stats: FeatureStats):
+        theta_array = np.asarray(theta, dtype=np.float64)
+        expected = 3 * len(FEATURE_NAMES) + 3
+        if theta_array.shape != (expected,):
+            raise ValueError(f"Expected {expected} controller parameters, got {theta_array.shape}")
+        split = 3 * len(FEATURE_NAMES)
+        self.matrix = theta_array[:split].reshape(3, len(FEATURE_NAMES))
+        self.bias = theta_array[split:]
+        self.stats = stats
+
+    def weights(self, features: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
+        standardized = self.stats.transform(features)
+        logits = self.matrix @ standardized + self.bias
+        logits = logits - logits.max()
+        exp_logits = np.exp(logits)
+        return exp_logits / exp_logits.sum()
+
+
+def initial_linear_theta(lexical_bias: float = 4.0, other_bias: float = -2.0) -> np.ndarray:
+    theta = np.zeros(3 * len(FEATURE_NAMES) + 3, dtype=np.float64)
+    theta[-3:] = [lexical_bias, other_bias, other_bias]
+    return theta
+
+
+def seed_everything(seed: int) -> None:
+    np.random.seed(seed)
+    torch.manual_seed(seed)
+    if torch.cuda.is_available():
+        torch.cuda.manual_seed_all(seed)
+
+
+def build_prompt(tokenizer: Any, question: str) -> tuple[str, torch.Tensor]:
+    instruction = (
+        "Solve the arithmetic problem carefully. Keep the reasoning inside the thinking region. "
+        "After </think>, return only the final number in the form \\boxed{number}.\n\n"
+        f"Problem: {question}"
+    )
+    rendered = tokenizer.apply_chat_template(
+        [{"role": "user", "content": instruction}],
+        tokenize=False,
+        add_generation_prompt=True,
+    )
+    if not rendered.endswith("<think>\n"):
+        rendered += "<think>\n"
+    tokenized = tokenizer(rendered, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False)
+    return rendered, tokenized.input_ids
+
+
+def extract_reference_answer(dataset_answer: str) -> str:
+    value = dataset_answer.split("####")[-1].strip().replace(",", "")
+    match = re.search(r"[-+]?\d+(?:\.\d+)?", value)
+    if not match:
+        raise ValueError(f"Could not extract numeric answer from {dataset_answer!r}")
+    return match.group(0)
+
+
+def extract_generated_answer(text: str) -> str | None:
+    boxed = re.findall(r"\\boxed\{\s*([-+]?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?)\s*\}", text)
+    if boxed:
+        return boxed[-1].replace(",", "")
+    numbers = re.findall(r"[-+]?\d+(?:[.,]\d+)?", text)
+    return numbers[-1].replace(",", "") if numbers else None
+
+
+def find_subsequence(sequence: Sequence[int], subsequence: Sequence[int]) -> int | None:
+    if not subsequence:
+        return 0
+    width = len(subsequence)
+    for index in range(len(sequence) - width + 1):
+        if list(sequence[index : index + width]) == list(subsequence):
+            return index
+    return None
+
+
+def cache_length(cache: Any) -> int:
+    if hasattr(cache, "get_seq_length"):
+        return int(cache.get_seq_length())
+    return int(cache[0][0].shape[-2])
+
+
+def reusable_cache(cache: Any) -> Any:
+    """Prefer immutable legacy tuples so one prefix can seed many rollouts."""
+
+    if hasattr(cache, "to_legacy_cache"):
+        return cache.to_legacy_cache()
+    return cache
+
+
+@torch.inference_mode()
+def initial_state(model: Any, input_ids: torch.Tensor) -> ModelState:
+    device = next(model.parameters()).device
+    input_ids = input_ids.to(device)
+    attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids)
+    outputs = model(
+        input_ids=input_ids,
+        attention_mask=attention_mask,
+        use_cache=True,
+        output_hidden_states=True,
+        return_dict=True,
+    )
+    return ModelState(
+        cache=reusable_cache(outputs.past_key_values),

+@torch.inference_mode()
+def advance_embedding(model: Any, state: ModelState, embedding_t1: torch.Tensor) -> ModelState:
+    """Process E_(t+1) with C_t and return h_(t+1), logits_(t+2), C_(t+1)."""

+    past_length = cache_length(state.cache)

+    attention_mask = torch.ones((1, past_length + 1), dtype=torch.long, device=device)
+    cache_position = torch.tensor([past_length], dtype=torch.long, device=device)
+    outputs = model(
+        inputs_embeds=inputs_embeds,
+        attention_mask=attention_mask,
+        past_key_values=state.cache,
+        cache_position=cache_position,
+        use_cache=True,
+        output_hidden_states=True,
+        return_dict=True,
+    )
+    return ModelState(
+        cache=reusable_cache(outputs.past_key_values),
+        logits_next=outputs.logits[0, -1].detach(),
+        hidden_t=outputs.hidden_states[-1][0, -1].detach(),

+def _as_eos_ids(tokenizer: Any) -> set[int]:
+    ids = tokenizer.eos_token_id
+    if ids is None:
+        return set()
+    if isinstance(ids, int):
+        return {ids}
+    return {int(item) for item in ids}

+def masked_reasoning_logits(
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    shadow_ids: Sequence[int],
+    close_ids: Sequence[int],
+    eos_ids: set[int],
+) -> torch.Tensor:
+    """Prevent the fixed-length shadow path from completing a terminator."""
+
+    masked = logits.float().clone()
+    for token_id in eos_ids:
+        masked[token_id] = -torch.inf
+
+    if len(close_ids) == 1:
+        masked[close_ids[0]] = -torch.inf
+    elif close_ids:
+        prefix = list(close_ids[:-1])
+        if len(shadow_ids) >= len(prefix) and list(shadow_ids[-len(prefix) :]) == prefix:
+            masked[close_ids[-1]] = -torch.inf
+    return masked
+

+def next_candidates(
+    model: Any,
+    tokenizer: Any,
+    logits: torch.Tensor,
+    shadow_ids: Sequence[int],
+    close_ids: Sequence[int],
+) -> CandidateSet:
+    masked = masked_reasoning_logits(logits, shadow_ids, close_ids, _as_eos_ids(tokenizer))
+    probabilities = torch.softmax(masked, dim=-1)
+    values, indices = torch.topk(probabilities, k=2)
+    y1, y2 = (int(indices[0]), int(indices[1]))
+    embedding_table = model.get_input_embeddings().weight
+    entropy = -(probabilities * torch.log(probabilities.clamp_min(1e-30))).sum()
+    vocabulary_size = probabilities.numel()
+    normalized_entropy = entropy / math.log(vocabulary_size)
+    effective_vocab = 1.0 / probabilities.square().sum()
+    return CandidateSet(
+        y1=y1,
+        y2=y2,
+        e1=embedding_table[y1].detach(),
+        e2=embedding_table[y2].detach(),
+        p1=float(values[0]),
+        p2=float(values[1]),
+        logit_margin=float(masked[y1] - masked[y2]),
+        entropy_normalized=float(normalized_entropy),
+        log_effective_vocab=float(torch.log(effective_vocab)),
+    )

+def hidden_for_variant(hidden_t: torch.Tensor, e1: torch.Tensor, variant: str) -> torch.Tensor:
+    if variant == "raw":
+        return hidden_t
+    if variant == "norm_matched":
+        return hidden_t * (torch.linalg.vector_norm(e1) / torch.linalg.vector_norm(hidden_t).clamp_min(1e-12))
+    raise ValueError(f"Unknown hidden-state variant: {variant}")

+def local_features(hidden_source: torch.Tensor, candidates: CandidateSet) -> np.ndarray:
+    h = hidden_source.float()
+    e1 = candidates.e1.float()
+    e2 = candidates.e2.float()
+    norm_h = torch.linalg.vector_norm(h)
+    norm_e1 = torch.linalg.vector_norm(e1)
+    row = np.asarray(
+        [
+            float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(h - e1)),
+            float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(h - e2)),
+            float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(e1 - e2)),
+            float(F.cosine_similarity(h, e1, dim=0)),
+            float(F.cosine_similarity(h, e2, dim=0)),
+            float(F.cosine_similarity(e1, e2, dim=0)),
+            candidates.logit_margin,
+            candidates.p1,
+            candidates.p2,
+            candidates.p1 + candidates.p2,
+            candidates.entropy_normalized,
+            candidates.log_effective_vocab,
+            float(torch.log((norm_h + 1e-12) / (norm_e1 + 1e-12))),
+        ],
+        dtype=np.float64,
+    )
+    if not np.all(np.isfinite(row)):
+        raise FloatingPointError(f"Non-finite controller features: {row}")
+    return row
+

+@torch.inference_mode()
+def run_reasoning(

+        matched_h = hidden_for_variant(state.hidden_t, candidates.e1, "norm_matched")

+        matched_row = local_features(matched_h, candidates)
+        raw_features.append(raw_row)
+        norm_matched_features.append(matched_row)

+        hidden_source = raw_h if hidden_variant == "raw" else matched_h

+        if policy.exact_lexical:

+        else:

+                tensor_weights[0] * candidates.e1
+                + tensor_weights[1] * candidates.e2
+                + tensor_weights[2] * hidden_source
+            )
+
+        drift = float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(transmitted.float() - candidates.e1.float()))

+        norm_entry = {
+            "hidden": float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(state.hidden_t.float())),
+            "e1": float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(candidates.e1.float())),
+            "e2": float(torch.linalg.vector_norm(candidates.e2.float())),
+        }
+        norm_rows.append(norm_entry)
+        if record_trace:
+            trace.append(
+                {
+                    "next_position": next_position,
+                    "y1": candidates.y1,
+                    "y2": candidates.y2,
+                    "token1": tokenizer.decode([candidates.y1]),
+                    "token2": tokenizer.decode([candidates.y2]),
+                    "weights": weights.tolist(),
+                    "drift": drift,
+                    "relative_drift": relative_drift,
+                    "p1": candidates.p1,
+                    "p2": candidates.p2,
+                    "entropy_normalized": candidates.entropy_normalized,
+                    "log_effective_vocab": candidates.log_effective_vocab,
+                }

+        state_after_reasoning=state,
+        trace=trace,

# Continuous-Drift CoT Probe

This repository is a small direction-finding experiment. It tests whether a frozen
`DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B` model can benefit when the next Chain-of-Thought
input is a convex mixture of its top two token embeddings and its current final
hidden state.

The first pass is intentionally lean:

1. verify that a one-token cached embedding loop reproduces greedy lexical decoding;
2. measure native reasoning lengths and hidden/token norm geometry;
3. compare a fixed-budget lexical run with a few static continuous mixtures; and
4. run a very small CMA-ES search only after the machinery passes those checks.

The detailed design and interpretation rules are in
[`Cot_Experiment.md`](Cot_Experiment.md).

## Run on the configured Colab CLI

From WSL, create a named T4 session, install requirements, upload the two Python
files, and execute the runner. Always stop the session afterward.

```bash
colab new -s cot-drift --gpu T4
colab install -s cot-drift -r /mnt/d/CoT/requirements-colab.txt
colab upload -s cot-drift /mnt/d/CoT/cot_drift.py /content/cot_drift.py
colab upload -s cot-drift /mnt/d/CoT/run_experiment.py /content/run_experiment.py
colab exec -s cot-drift -f /mnt/d/CoT/run_experiment.py --timeout 1800
colab download -s cot-drift /content/cot_drift_results.json /mnt/d/CoT/artifacts/cot_drift_results.json
colab stop -s cot-drift
```

The default runner is a cheap engineering smoke test with built-in arithmetic
problems, eight controlled positions, static controls, and no CMA generations.
Once that passes, use the command-line flags at the bottom of
[`run_experiment.py`](run_experiment.py) for a GSM8K screen or CMA run.

## Important interpretation rule

The native greedy baseline is not the fixed-budget lexical control. The causal
comparison is between fixed-budget lexical and fixed-budget drift, which use the
same cache loop, termination mask, and reasoning budget. Native generation is an
external reference for the effect of that harness.

"""Colab entrypoint for the continuous-drift CoT direction-finding probe."""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import json
import os
import platform
import sys
import time
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any

import numpy as np
import torch
import transformers
from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

from cot_drift import (
    FeatureStats,
    LexicalPolicy,
    LinearPolicy,
    Problem,
    StaticPolicy,
    build_prompt,
    cached_lexical_parity,
    evaluate_policy,
    extract_reference_answer,
    initial_linear_theta,
    initial_state,
    native_greedy,
    run_reasoning,
    seed_everything,
    summarize_norms,
)


BUILTIN_PROBLEMS = [
    Problem("A box holds 18 red marbles and 7 blue marbles. Five marbles are removed. How many remain?", "20"),
    Problem("Maya buys 4 notebooks at 6 dollars each and pays with 30 dollars. How much change does she receive?", "6"),
    Problem("A train travels 45 miles per hour for 3 hours. How many miles does it travel?", "135"),
    Problem("There are 8 tables with 5 chairs each. Six chairs are removed. How many chairs remain?", "34"),
    Problem("Noah reads 12 pages on Monday, 15 on Tuesday, and twice Monday's amount on Wednesday. How many pages total?", "51"),
    Problem("A baker made 72 rolls and packed them equally into 9 bags. How many rolls are in each bag?", "8"),
]


def parse_args() -> argparse.Namespace:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
    parser.add_argument("--model-id", default="deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B")
    parser.add_argument("--dataset", choices=("builtin", "gsm8k"), default="builtin")
    parser.add_argument("--fixed-steps", type=int, default=8)
    parser.add_argument("--calibration-examples", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--search-examples", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--eval-examples", type=int, default=2)
    parser.add_argument("--native-max-new-tokens", type=int, default=128)
    parser.add_argument("--final-max-new-tokens", type=int, default=24)
    parser.add_argument("--cma-generations", type=int, default=0)
    parser.add_argument("--cma-popsize", type=int, default=6)
    parser.add_argument("--cma-sigma", type=float, default=0.35)
    parser.add_argument("--controller-variant", choices=("raw", "norm_matched"), default="norm_matched")
    parser.add_argument("--seed", type=int, default=17)
    parser.add_argument("--output", default="/content/cot_drift_results.json")
    parser.add_argument("--skip-native", action="store_true")
    return parser.parse_args()


def load_problems(args: argparse.Namespace) -> list[Problem]:
    total = args.calibration_examples + args.search_examples + args.eval_examples
    if args.dataset == "builtin":
        if total > len(BUILTIN_PROBLEMS):
            raise ValueError(f"Built-in mode has {len(BUILTIN_PROBLEMS)} problems; requested {total}")
        return BUILTIN_PROBLEMS[:total]

    from datasets import load_dataset

    dataset = load_dataset("openai/gsm8k", "main", split="test").shuffle(seed=args.seed)
    rows = dataset.select(range(total))
    return [Problem(row["question"], extract_reference_answer(row["answer"])) for row in rows]


def load_frozen_model(model_id: str) -> tuple[Any, Any]:
    if not torch.cuda.is_available():
        raise RuntimeError("This experiment expects a CUDA Colab runtime; no GPU was detected")
    tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
    model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
        model_id,
        torch_dtype=torch.float16,
        device_map={"": 0},
        low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
    )
    model.eval()
    for parameter in model.parameters():
        parameter.requires_grad_(False)
    if tokenizer.pad_token_id is None:
        tokenizer.pad_token_id = tokenizer.eos_token_id
    return model, tokenizer


def prepare_examples(model: Any, tokenizer: Any, problems: list[Problem]) -> tuple[list[tuple[Problem, Any]], list[str], list[torch.Tensor]]:
    examples = []
    prompts = []
    input_ids_rows = []
    for problem in problems:
        prompt, input_ids = build_prompt(tokenizer, problem.question)
        examples.append((problem, initial_state(model, input_ids)))
        prompts.append(prompt)
        input_ids_rows.append(input_ids)
    return examples, prompts, input_ids_rows


def compact_evaluation(evaluation: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    return {
        "mean_loss": evaluation["mean_loss"],
        "exact_match": evaluation["exact_match"],
        "rows": [
            {
                key: value
                for key, value in row.items()
                if key in {"answer", "loss", "generated", "predicted", "correct"}
            }
            for row in evaluation["rows"]
        ],
    }


def run_static_screen(model: Any, tokenizer: Any, eval_examples: list[tuple[Problem, Any]], args: argparse.Namespace) -> dict[str, Any]:
    conditions = [
        ("lexical", LexicalPolicy(), "raw"),
        ("static_e1e2_90_10", StaticPolicy([0.90, 0.10, 0.00]), "raw"),
        ("static_e1h_raw_95_05", StaticPolicy([0.95, 0.00, 0.05]), "raw"),
        ("static_e1h_matched_90_10", StaticPolicy([0.90, 0.00, 0.10]), "norm_matched"),
        ("static_full_matched_80_10_10", StaticPolicy([0.80, 0.10, 0.10]), "norm_matched"),
    ]
    results: dict[str, Any] = {}
    for name, policy, variant in conditions:
        print(f"[screen] {name}", flush=True)
        evaluation = evaluate_policy(
            model,
            tokenizer,
            eval_examples,
            args.fixed_steps,
            policy,
            variant,
            generate_answers=False,
        )
        results[name] = compact_evaluation(evaluation)

    best_name = min(results, key=lambda item: results[item]["mean_loss"])
    best_policy_entry = next(item for item in conditions if item[0] == best_name)
    generated = evaluate_policy(
        model,
        tokenizer,
        eval_examples,
        args.fixed_steps,
        best_policy_entry[1],
        best_policy_entry[2],
        generate_answers=True,
    )
    results[best_name] = compact_evaluation(generated)
    return {"best": best_name, "conditions": results}


def run_cma(
    model: Any,
    tokenizer: Any,
    search_examples: list[tuple[Problem, Any]],
    eval_examples: list[tuple[Problem, Any]],
    stats: FeatureStats,
    args: argparse.Namespace,
) -> dict[str, Any] | None:
    if args.cma_generations <= 0:
        return None

    import cma

    initial = initial_linear_theta()
    options = {
        "bounds": [-8.0, 8.0],
        "popsize": args.cma_popsize,
        "seed": args.seed,
        "verbose": -9,
    }
    strategy = cma.CMAEvolutionStrategy(initial, args.cma_sigma, options)
    history = []

    for generation in range(args.cma_generations):
        candidates = strategy.ask()
        losses = []
        for candidate_index, theta in enumerate(candidates):
            policy = LinearPolicy(theta, stats)
            evaluation = evaluate_policy(
                model,
                tokenizer,
                search_examples,
                args.fixed_steps,
                policy,
                args.controller_variant,
                generate_answers=False,
            )
            loss = evaluation["mean_loss"]
            losses.append(loss)
            print(
                f"[cma] generation={generation + 1} candidate={candidate_index + 1}/{len(candidates)} loss={loss:.6f}",
                flush=True,
            )
        strategy.tell(candidates, losses)
        history.append(
            {
                "generation": generation + 1,
                "best_generation_loss": float(min(losses)),
                "mean_generation_loss": float(np.mean(losses)),
            }
        )

    champion_theta = np.asarray(strategy.result.xbest, dtype=np.float64)
    champion = LinearPolicy(champion_theta, stats)
    validation = evaluate_policy(
        model,
        tokenizer,
        eval_examples,
        args.fixed_steps,
        champion,
        args.controller_variant,
        generate_answers=True,
    )
    return {
        "variant": args.controller_variant,
        "parameter_count": int(champion_theta.size),
        "theta": champion_theta.tolist(),
        "search_best_loss": float(strategy.result.fbest),
        "history": history,
        "evaluation": compact_evaluation(validation),
    }


def main() -> None:
    args = parse_args()
    seed_everything(args.seed)
    started = time.time()
    output_path = Path(args.output)
    output_path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)

    print(f"[setup] loading {args.model_id}", flush=True)
    model, tokenizer = load_frozen_model(args.model_id)
    problems = load_problems(args)
    examples, prompts, input_ids_rows = prepare_examples(model, tokenizer, problems)

    calibration_end = args.calibration_examples
    search_end = calibration_end + args.search_examples
    calibration = examples[:calibration_end]
    search = examples[calibration_end:search_end]
    evaluation = examples[search_end:]

    print("[check] cached lexical parity", flush=True)
    parity = cached_lexical_parity(model, tokenizer, input_ids_rows[0], steps=min(4, args.fixed_steps))
    if not parity["all_argmax_match"]:
        raise RuntimeError(f"Cached lexical loop failed parity: {parity}")

    native_rows = []
    if not args.skip_native:
        print("[calibration] native greedy lengths", flush=True)
        for index in range(args.calibration_examples):
            native = native_greedy(model, tokenizer, input_ids_rows[index], args.native_max_new_tokens)
            native_rows.append(
                {
                    "reasoning_tokens": native["reasoning_tokens"],
                    "right_censored": native["right_censored"],
                    "generated_tokens": native["generated_tokens"],
                    "predicted": native["predicted"],
                    "answer": problems[index].answer,
                    "correct": native["predicted"] == problems[index].answer,
                    "text_preview": native["text"][:1000],
                }
            )

    print("[calibration] features and norm geometry", flush=True)
    raw_feature_rows = []
    matched_feature_rows = []
    norm_rows = []
    for _, prefix in calibration:
        trajectory = run_reasoning(
            model,
            tokenizer,
            prefix,
            args.fixed_steps,
            LexicalPolicy(),
            "raw",
            record_trace=False,
        )
        raw_feature_rows.extend(trajectory.raw_features)
        matched_feature_rows.extend(trajectory.norm_matched_features)
        norm_rows.extend(trajectory.norm_rows)
    raw_stats = FeatureStats.fit(raw_feature_rows)
    matched_stats = FeatureStats.fit(matched_feature_rows)
    selected_stats = raw_stats if args.controller_variant == "raw" else matched_stats

    static_screen = run_static_screen(model, tokenizer, evaluation, args)
    cma_result = run_cma(model, tokenizer, search, evaluation, selected_stats, args)

    result = {
        "config": vars(args),
        "environment": {
            "python": sys.version,
            "platform": platform.platform(),
            "torch": torch.__version__,
            "transformers": transformers.__version__,
            "cuda_device": torch.cuda.get_device_name(0),
        },
        "tokenization": {
            "prompt_preview": prompts[0][-1000:],
            "prompt_tokens": int(input_ids_rows[0].shape[1]),
            "think_close_ids": tokenizer.encode("</think>", add_special_tokens=False),
            "forced_boundary_ids": tokenizer.encode("</think>\n", add_special_tokens=False),
        },
        "parity": parity,
        "native_calibration": native_rows,
        "norm_geometry": summarize_norms(norm_rows),
        "feature_stats": {
            "raw": raw_stats.to_json(),
            "norm_matched": matched_stats.to_json(),
        },
        "static_screen": static_screen,
        "cma": cma_result,
        "elapsed_seconds": time.time() - started,
    }
    output_path.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
    print(json.dumps({
        "output": str(output_path),
        "parity": parity,
        "norm_hidden_over_e1": result["norm_geometry"].get("hidden_over_e1"),
        "static_best": static_screen["best"],
        "static_losses": {
            name: row["mean_loss"] for name, row in static_screen["conditions"].items()

import numpy as np

from cot_drift import (
    FEATURE_NAMES,
    FeatureStats,
    LinearPolicy,
    StaticPolicy,
    extract_generated_answer,
    extract_reference_answer,
    find_subsequence,
    initial_linear_theta,
)


def test_answer_extractors():
    assert extract_reference_answer("work\n#### 1,234") == "1234"
    assert extract_generated_answer("answer: \\boxed{-42}") == "-42"


def test_find_subsequence():
    assert find_subsequence([1, 2, 3, 4], [2, 3]) == 1
    assert find_subsequence([1, 2], [3]) is None


def test_static_policy_normalizes():
    assert np.allclose(StaticPolicy([8, 1, 1]).weights(np.zeros(1)), [0.8, 0.1, 0.1])


def test_linear_policy_starts_near_lexical():
    rows = [np.zeros(len(FEATURE_NAMES)), np.ones(len(FEATURE_NAMES))]
    stats = FeatureStats.fit(rows)
    policy = LinearPolicy(initial_linear_theta(), stats)
    weights = policy.weights(np.zeros(len(FEATURE_NAMES)))
    assert weights[0] > 0.99
    assert np.isclose(weights.sum(), 1.0)

# Colab CLI

A command-line interface for Google Colab. Provision high-performance CPU, GPU, and TPU runtimes, execute local code, manage remote files, and orchestrate automated cloud pipelines — directly from your terminal.

Designed to support seamless developer productivity, headless automation, and AI agent integrations.

demo.mov

Note

Platform support: the Colab CLI currently supports Linux and macOS only. Windows is not supported at this time.

Tip

Looking for in-notebook, interactive agent-assisted coding instead of a terminal workflow? See the Colab MCP Server.

* * *

## Key Features

  * Instant VM Provisioning: Spin up CPU, GPU (T4, L4, G4, H100, A100), or TPU (v5e1, v6e1) runtimes in seconds.
  * Robust Code Execution: Run local Python scripts, Jupyter Notebooks (`.ipynb`), or piped `stdin` code; launch interactive REPLs or raw TTY console shells.
  * Ephemeral Job Runner (`colab run`): Provision a fresh VM, execute a local script with forwarded arguments, retrieve output files, and automatically tear down the runtime in a single command.
  * Automatic Keep-Alive: Built-in background daemon automatically prevents idle VM termination, keeping resource allocations active without requiring open browser tabs.
  * Seamless Workspace Automation: Mount Google Drive, authenticate Google Cloud Platform (GCP) credentials, and install dependencies with high-performance `uv` package management.
  * State & Log Archival: Inspect local session states or export interactive history logs to standard Jupyter Notebooks, Markdown, or structured JSONL.

* * *

## Installation

Install the package using `uv` (recommended) or standard `pip`:
    
    # Using uv (recommended)
    uv tool install google-colab-cli
    
    # Using pip
    pip install google-colab-cli

* * *

## Quick Start

Run a CPU-based VM runtime, execute some code, and clean up:
    
    # 1. Provision a new session
    colab new
    
    # 2. Execute code from stdin
    echo "print('Hello from Google Colab!')" | colab exec
    
    # 3. Stop and release the VM resource
    colab stop

Note

When only one session is active, you can omit the `-s, --session` option; the CLI automatically knows it.

* * *

## Command Index

Run `colab <command> --help` to view specific options, defaults, and detailed help.

### Session Management

Command  | Description
--- | ---
`colab new [-s NAME] [--gpu GPU] [--tpu TPU]`  | Allocate a new CPU, GPU, or TPU VM runtime
`colab sessions`  | List all active sessions currently active on the backend
`colab status [-s NAME]`  | Display hardware, status, and local metadata for active sessions
`colab restart-kernel [-s NAME]`  | Restart the active session's Jupyter kernel
`colab stop [-s NAME]`  | Terminate a session VM and tear down its keep-alive daemon
`colab url [-s NAME] [--open]`  | Print or open a browser URL connecting to the active session

### Execution

Command  | Description
--- | ---
`colab run [--gpu GPU] [--tpu TPU] [--keep] SCRIPT [ARGS...]`  | Run a local script on a fresh VM, forwarding arguments, then release it
`colab exec [-s NAME] [-f FILE] [--output-image PATH]`  | Execute Python code from stdin, a local `.py` file, or a `.ipynb` notebook
`colab repl [-s NAME] [--output-image PATH]`  | Start an interactive Python REPL on the VM (exits cleanly on piped EOF)
`colab console [-s NAME]`  | Connect to a raw interactive TTY shell (tmux) on the remote VM
`colab ssh [-s NAME] [--proxy-mode] [-i KEY]`  | Open an SSH shell to the runtime over WebSocket, or act as an OpenSSH `ProxyCommand` bridge for IDE remote-dev

### File Operations

Command  | Description
--- | ---
`colab ls [-s NAME] [PATH]`  | List remote files on the VM
`colab upload [-s NAME] LOCAL REMOTE`  | Upload a local file to the VM filesystem
`colab download [-s NAME] REMOTE LOCAL`  | Download a remote file from the VM filesystem
`colab rm [-s NAME] PATH`  | Delete a remote file on the VM filesystem
`colab edit [-s NAME] PATH`  | Edit a remote file in-place using your local `$EDITOR`

### Automation & Utilities

Command  | Description
--- | ---
`colab auth [-s NAME]`  | Authenticate the VM for GCP services (BigQuery, GCS, etc.)
`colab drivemount [-s NAME] [PATH]`  | Mount Google Drive on the VM (default: `/content/drive`)
`colab install [-s NAME] [-r FILE | PKG...]`  | Install packages on the VM using `uv` (falls back to `pip`)
`colab log [-s NAME] [-n N] [-o FILE]`  | View or export session history (`.ipynb`, `.md`, `.txt`, `.jsonl`)
`colab pay`  | Open the Colab subscription page to manage compute units
`colab version`  | Print the installed version of the CLI
`colab update [--install]`  | Check for a newer release (and optionally upgrade the CLI in place)

### Global Options

  * `--auth {oauth2,adc}` — Authentication strategy for the Colab API (default: `adc`).
  * `-c, --client-oauth-config PATH` — Path to public OAuth client credentials configuration (default: `~/.colab-cli-oauth-config.json`).
  * `--config PATH` — Path to local session metadata storage (default: `~/.config/colab-cli/sessions.json`).
  * `--logtostderr` — Direct debug logging output to stderr.

* * *

## Practical Examples

### Accelerator Training with Checkpoint Retrieval

Provision an A100 GPU, install requirements, run a local training script, retrieve the resulting model weights, and terminate the VM:
    
    colab new -s trainer --gpu A100
    colab install -s trainer torch transformers
    colab exec -s trainer -f train.py
    colab download -s trainer checkpoints/model.bin ./model.bin
    colab stop -s trainer

### Workspace Notebook Execution with Drive Integration

Mount Google Drive, run a local notebook against the VM kernel (outputs are written back into `report_output.ipynb`), export a Markdown log of the execution, and clean up:
    
    colab new -s analysis
    colab drivemount -s analysis
    colab exec -s analysis -f report.ipynb
    colab log -s analysis -o execution_log.md
    colab stop -s analysis

* * *

## Usage Notes

  * TTY Requirements: The interactive commands `repl` and `console` require a local TTY. When running inside automated scripts or pipelines, make sure to pipe stdin (e.g., `echo "print(1)" | colab repl`) to trigger non-interactive execution modes.
  * Transparent Code Execution: When calling `colab exec -f file.py`, the CLI reads the file locally and transmits its content to the remote kernel. You do not need to manually upload files before execution.
  * Storage & State Paths: Session tokens and metadata are stored at `~/.config/colab-cli/sessions.json`. Global CLI settings are located at `~/.config/colab-cli/settings.json`. These can be customized or isolated via the global `--config` flag.

### Ephemeral Accelerator Jobs

Use `colab run` to run a local script on dedicated hardware without manual session lifecycle management. The CLI handles provisioning, script execution, and immediate VM teardown automatically:
    
    # Run train.py on a T4 GPU and release the VM on completion
    colab run --gpu T4 train.py

### Shebang Execution Support

To execute a local file directly on a remote accelerator, place the `colab run` interpreter in the shebang line:
    
    #!/usr/bin/env -S colab run --gpu L4 --keep
    import torch
    
    print("L4 GPU Available:", torch.cuda.is_available())
    print("Device Name:", torch.cuda.get_device_name(0))

Make the script executable (`chmod +x script.py`) and run it: `./script.py`. The `--keep` option tells the CLI to preserve the session VM on completion so you can re-execute or inspect logs.

# Colab CLI: Agent Guidelines

## Architecture Overview

  * CLI: Modular `Typer` based entry point in `cli.py` with subcommands in `commands/`.
  * Common: `common.py` centralizes shared `State` (lazy-loading) and session resolution.
  * Client: `ColabClient` handles API interactions (assignment, unassignment).
  * Auth: `auth.py` exposes a single `get_credentials(config_path, provider)` facade that dispatches on the `AuthProvider` enum. Two providers are supported, selected via the global `--auth=oauth2|adc` flag (default `oauth2`):
    * `oauth2`: public `google-auth-oauthlib` `InstalledAppFlow`, token cached at `~/.config/colab-cli/token.json`. Reads the client OAuth config from `-c/--client-oauth-config` (default `~/.colab-cli-oauth-config.json`), falling back to the bundled `src/colab_cli/oauth_config.json` resource (re-added in PR #41 / `9f44fe2`, 2026-05-29 — the earlier "removed in `20eb88e`" note was stale/incorrect; the file exists and `auth.py:_get_google_auth_credentials` loads it via `importlib.resources`). Service-account / GCE / GKE / impersonated creds get the right scopes transparently via `with_scopes`.
  * Backend Hosts: Two distinct backends with different requirements:
    * `colab.research.google.com` (session backend / `tun/m/...`): accepts the `userinfo.email` scope. Handles assign, unassign, the contents API, and keep-alive (see below).
    * Keep-alive (2026-06-15, issue #14): keep-alive is a Tunnel Frontend (TFE) HTTP ping — `GET https://colab.research.google.com/tun/m/<endpoint>/keep-alive/` with header `X-Colab-Tunnel: Google`, authenticated by the user's own Gaia bearer token (same host/credential as `assign`). TFE records `LastActiveTime` before forwarding, refreshing the idle timer. The VM usually doesn't answer on this path, so the request commonly read-times-out even on success — `client.keep_alive_assignment` therefore catches `requests.exceptions.ReadTimeout` and treats it as success, while genuine HTTP errors (e.g. 404 for a deleted assignment) propagate. This mirrors the official `colab-vscode` extension's `sendKeepAlive` (`src/colab/client.ts`). DO NOT revert to the `colab.pa.googleapis.com` `RuntimeService/KeepAliveAssignment` RPC: that RPC requires the caller to be a `serviceusage` consumer of Colab's internal project `1014160490159`, which no ordinary user account is, so it returned HTTP 403 `USER_PROJECT_DENIED` for every external user (issue #14) and silently idle-pruned their sessions within minutes. The browser only made that RPC work by riding the user's `google.com` cookie through an internal cookie-proxy (`colab.clients6.google.com`), which a headless bearer-token CLI cannot use. Verified live 2026-06-15 with a third-party account (the RPC 403'd; the tunnel ping succeeded and kept the VM alive).
  * Runtime: `ColabRuntime` wraps `jupyter-kernel-client` for execution.
  * State:
    * `StateStore` persists session metadata in `~/.config/colab-cli/sessions.json`.
    * Persistent settings are in `~/.config/colab-cli/settings.json`.
  * History: `HistoryLogger` records structured events in `~/.config/colab-cli/history/*.jsonl`.

## Core Mandates

  * Minimalism: Favor standard library where possible (e.g., `urllib`) while utilizing `Typer` for CLI ergonomics.

  * Piping: Always consider piped input (`stdin`) vs. interactive TTY.

  * Trace Alignment: When implementing new endpoints, validate against captured browser traces (HAR files).

  * TDD (Test-Driven Development): Always implement tests first. Verify they fail before implementing the solution to make them pass. Every design must include a testing strategy and specific test cases.

  * Jupyter Protocol Deviations: Google Colab uses custom extensions to the Jupyter protocol. Examples include `colab_request` messages over the `iopub` channel and `input_reply` wrapping `colab_reply` payloads on the `stdin` channel. These require monkey-patching or specialized handlers within `jupyter-kernel-client` (e.g., `wsclient.kernel_socket.on_message` interceptors).

  * Integration Testing: Unit tests and mocks are not enough. Before declaring any feature complete, you MUST perform a real-world, end-to-end integration test against a live Colab environment using the CLI. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Approach

### 1. Authentication (`colab auth`)

  * Action: Execute code on the VM to trigger user-interactive authentication using the classic Gcloud fallback.
  * Code: `python import os os.environ['USE_AUTH_EPHEM'] = '0' from google.colab import auth auth.authenticate_user()`
  * Handling: Setting `USE_AUTH_EPHEM` to `'0'` forces the kernel to print a standard `gcloud` verification URL and trigger an `input_request` message on the `iopub` channel. The CLI intercepts this via a `stdin_hook` and prompts the user locally, returning the code to unlock the kernel.

### 2. Package Installation (`colab install`)

  * Action: Execute `pip` on the VM.
  * Code: `python import sys, subprocess subprocess.check_call([sys.executable, "-m", "pip", "install", "..."])`
  * Requirements File: Upload `requirements.txt` if provided with `-r` and then run `pip install -r`.

### 3. Drive Mounting (`colab drivemount`)

  * Action: Execute `drive.mount()` and transparently proxy Colab's proprietary credential propagation flow.
  * Code: `python from google.colab import drive drive.mount('/content/drive')`
  * Handling: Because `drivefs` enforces the ephemeral side-channel propagation (`colab_request` over websocket), the CLI intercepts these messages using `ColabRuntime.colab_request_hook`. When intercepted, the CLI automatically interacts with the Colab backend (`/tun/m/credentials-propagation/`), prompts the user with the Google OAuth consent URL if needed, and dispatches the required `colab_reply` message to the `stdin` channel to unlock the kernel thread.
  * Timeout: The kernel is silent (no iopub traffic) the entire time the user is OAuthing in their browser. To avoid the upstream 10s `jupyter_kernel_client` default raising `TimeoutError` mid-flow, this subcommand passes `timeout=INTERACTIVE_AUTOMATION_TIMEOUT_SEC` (600s) to `ColabRuntime.execute_code`. Same applies to `colab auth`.

### 4. Logging and Notebook Capture (`colab log`)

  * Action: Capture the session's command history and outputs.
  * Storage: Maintain a local JSON-L file of all major operations, executions, and stdin interactions in `~/.config/colab-cli/history/<session_name>.jsonl`.

### 2. Session Status (`colab status`)

  * API: `/api/sessions` or querying the kernel for resource usage via a special "status" message.

# Exploratory run notes

These are engineering and direction-finding runs, not benchmark claims.

## What passed

- The cached one-embedding loop matched the uncached greedy argmax at every
  checked position. FP16 logits differed by at most about 0.03 without changing
  the selected token.
- The tokenizer represents `</think>` as the single token `151649`; the forced
  `</think>\n` boundary is `[151649, 198]`.
- KV-cache reuse works with the current native Transformers cache object.
- The 42-parameter controller completed one CMA-ES generation end to end.

## Geometry

Across the calibration traces, the raw final hidden-state norm was roughly
73--79 times the top-1 input-embedding norm. A raw 5% hidden-state mixture was
therefore not a small intervention and performed very poorly. This validates the
decision to compare raw and per-step norm-matched hidden states.

## Tiny static screens

| Data / budget | Lexical loss | Best tested static loss | Winner |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| Two handwritten items, \(T=8\) | 2.2121 | 2.0722 | 90% \(e_1\) / 10% norm-matched \(h\) |
| Two handwritten items, \(T=128\) | 2.1251 | 1.9840 | 90% \(e_1\) / 10% norm-matched \(h\) |
| Four shuffled GSM8K items, \(T=128\) | 2.0907 | 2.0907 | Lexical |

On the four GSM8K examples, the tested full norm-matched mixture beat lexical on
two examples and lost on two; the losses were larger, so its mean was worse
(2.4899). This is compatible with the controller premise: continuous movement
can help, but a static global coefficient does not know where it is safe.

Exact-match generations are secondary in these smoke files. Short fixed budgets
and capped final generation sometimes leave the model continuing an explanation
after the forced boundary. The primary screening number here is teacher-forced
target-token loss.

## Files

- `cot_drift_smoke_static.json`: initial \(T=8\) static screen and native-length
  calibration (native reasoning lengths were 81 and 126 tokens).
- `cot_drift_smoke_cma.json`: one-generation CMA-ES plumbing check.
- `cot_drift_length128_static.json`: handwritten \(T=128\) screen.
- `cot_drift_gsm8k_static.json`: four-example GSM8K \(T=128\) screen.

content.text:
Setup is working, and the first evidence supports pursuing a dynamic controller rather than a universal static mixture.

Key observations:

- Cached decoding matched greedy argmax at every checked step.
- Raw hidden-state norms were roughly 73–79× token-embedding norms.
- On two handwritten problems at \(T=128\), norm-matched \(e_1/h\) improved loss from 2.1251 to 1.9840.
- On four GSM8K problems, lexical won overall. However, the full norm-matched mixture helped two problems and hurt two—useful evidence that drift may need context-sensitive gating.
- A 42-parameter CMA-ES controller completed an end-to-end plumbing run. That run is only an implementation check.

The implementation is in [cot_drift.py](D:/CoT/cot_drift.py:246), with the runner in [run_experiment.py](D:/CoT/run_experiment.py:148), the generated [Colab notebook](D:/CoT/notebooks/Continuous_Drift_Experiment.ipynb), and an automated [PowerShell-to-Colab launcher](D:/CoT/scripts/run_colab_job.ps1:1). Results are summarized in [artifacts/README.md](D:/CoT/artifacts/README.md:22).

- 4 tests passed.
- Notebook structure validated.
- All four result artifacts parse correctly.
- No Colab sessions remain active.
- Public Hugging Face assets downloaded without copying credentials.

- `--format` — Output format: `--format json` (or `--json`) or `--format table` (default).

## Mounting repos as local filesystems

To mount Hub repositories or buckets as local filesystems — no download, no copy, no waiting — use `hf-mount`. Files are fetched on demand. GitHub: https://github.com/huggingface/hf-mount

- `hf-mount start --hf-token $HF_TOKEN bucket myuser/my-bucket /tmp/data` — mount a bucket (read-write)
- `hf-mount status` / `hf-mount stop /tmp/data` — list or unmount

- Use `hf <command> --help` for full options, descriptions, usage, and real-world examples
- Authenticate with `HF_TOKEN` env var (recommended) or with `--token`
- Update the CLI with `hf update` (uses the correct command for the detected install method)

---
name: hf-cli
description: "Hugging Face Hub CLI (`hf`) for downloading, uploading, and managing models, datasets, spaces, buckets, repos, papers, jobs, and more on the Hugging Face Hub. Use when: handling authentication; managing local cache; managing Hugging Face Buckets; running or scheduling jobs on Hugging Face infrastructure; managing Hugging Face repos; discussions and pull requests; browsing models, datasets and spaces; reading, searching, or browsing academic papers; managing collections; querying datasets; configuring spaces; setting up webhooks; or deploying and managing HF Inference Endpoints. Make sure to use this skill whenever the user mentions 'hf', 'huggingface', 'Hugging Face', 'huggingface-cli', or 'hugging face cli', or wants to do anything related to the Hugging Face ecosystem and to AI and ML in general. Also use for cloud storage needs like training checkpoints, data pipelines, or agent traces. Use even if the user doesn't explicitly ask for a CLI command. Replaces the deprecated `huggingface-cli`."
---

Install: `curl -LsSf https://hf.co/cli/install.sh | bash -s`.

The Hugging Face Hub CLI tool `hf` is available. IMPORTANT: The `hf` command replaces the deprecated `huggingface-cli` command.

Use `hf --help` to view available functions. Note that auth commands are now all under `hf auth` e.g. `hf auth whoami`.

Generated with `huggingface_hub v1.27.0`. Run `hf skills add --force` to regenerate.

## Commands

- `hf cp SRC` — Copy files between local paths, repositories, and buckets. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf download REPO_ID` — Download files from the Hub. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --revision TEXT --include TEXT --exclude TEXT --cache-dir TEXT --local-dir TEXT --force-download --dry-run --max-workers INTEGER --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf env` — Print information about the environment. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf sync` — Sync files between local directory and a bucket. `[--delete --ignore-times --ignore-sizes --plan TEXT --apply TEXT --dry-run --include TEXT --exclude TEXT --filter-from TEXT --existing --ignore-existing --verbose --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf update` — Update the `hf` CLI to the latest version. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf upload REPO_ID` — Upload a file or a folder to the Hub. Recommended for single-commit uploads. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --revision TEXT --private --include TEXT --exclude TEXT --delete TEXT --commit-message TEXT --commit-description TEXT --create-pr --every FLOAT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf upload-large-folder REPO_ID LOCAL_PATH` — [Deprecated] Upload a large folder to the Hub. Use `hf upload` instead. `[--type [model|dataset|space] --revision TEXT --private --include TEXT --exclude TEXT --num-workers INTEGER --no-report --no-bars --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf version` — Print information about the hf version. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

### `hf auth` — Manage authentication (login, logout, etc.).

- `hf auth list` — List all stored access tokens. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf auth login` — Login from your browser, or using a token from huggingface.co/settings/tokens. `[--add-to-git-credential --force --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf auth logout` — Logout from a specific token. `[--token-name TEXT --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf auth switch` — Switch between access tokens. `[--token-name TEXT --add-to-git-credential --format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf auth token` — Print the current access token to stdout. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`
- `hf auth whoami` — Find out which huggingface.co account you are logged in as. `[--format [auto|human|agent|json|quiet]]`

### `hf buckets` — Commands to interact with buckets.

## Common options
